keyFindings.description: suggestionsBehindLock (lines 294-303) counts any backend blocked by the holder, and the seeded spec's document settlement (scheduled by POST /api/v1/issues, settle 20 ms in newTestServer) queues behind both the asks and issues locks, so neither test proves the suggestion call waited. Reproduced with a go test -overlay mutant that, for the two probes' askIDs only, sleeps 2 s and returns Missing without any query: both tests PASS 10 of 10; a pg_stat_activity overlay shows the waiters were the settlement's asks select and 'select coalesce(i.closed_at is null, true) from artifacts a left join issues i ...'. The tester's MUT=earlyslow control did not catch this because it also slept inside the issue-creation handler, which let settlement finish before the lock was taken. Fix: make the observed waiter the call's own (quiesce or postpone settlement before locking, or attribute the waiter to the step's statement), then re-run the negative controls and correct the E2E lines' claims.

consideredNotDefects: Non-empty Missing accepted for any failure (deep review finding 2): reproduced only with lock_timeout added to the test database URL; storetest's database sets no lock_timeout or statement_timeout, and the lock is released only after the answer is received, so once the waiter is the call's own query only its context can end it. Plan decision 5 deliberately asserts Missing without its text.
